answer: Beacon-Ledger Physical Anchor. Each identity must publish a live beacon from a dedicated hardware module co-located with its host, stamped with that module's factory key and a basalt-core tamper sensor reading. The ledger admits an identity only if consecutive beacons show unbroken sensor continuity; a hollow replay or cloned key breaks the chain. An attacker faking N identities must physically own N modules and keep them powered and co-located, paying hardware, shipping, and continuous power costs per identity rather than a one-time fee.
